audit_findings.title: Post-close capital structure is absent from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.9 billion acquisition price, equal to 49.3% of the $3.852 billion base equity value; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE omits RUCKUS earnings, term-loan interest and integration costs, while the bridge retains pre-close cash and debt rather than the post-close balance sheet.
audit_findings.evidence: However, we may require external financing were we to complete a significant acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the valuation is dated after the July 1 closing but combines legacy OE with a June 28 balance sheet. The omitted target earnings could increase value, while acquisition funding, interest, integration costs and cash consumption could decrease it. At roughly half of the stated base equity value, the transaction is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 1 closing statement, term-loan principal and fees, cash used, assumed liabilities, target historical financials and integration forecasts; then rerun OE, shares and the bridge on one consistent post-close perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital expenditure may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 capex was $136.2 million versus $63.8 million depreciation, a $72.4 million gap equal to 29.0% of $249.4 million anchor OE; the maintenance portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any capital expenditure required to sustain existing operations must be deducted in OE; classifying it as growth raises the OE anchor and every scenario value.
audit_findings.evidence: Investing activities for 2025 included $136.2 million for capital expenditures, partially offset by cash from business acquisitions and asset sales of $7.7 million and $0.2 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed numbers demonstrate that capex substantially exceeded depreciation, but they do not establish how much of the excess was maintenance rather than growth. The possible adjustment is large relative to anchor OE, yet the record cannot establish the amount or materiality of an actual error.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile several years of capex by plant replacement, corporate IT, capitalized software, modernization and capacity expansion; rerun the OE series and valuation using the evidenced maintenance component.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: December 2025 net funded deficit was $40.140 million ($20.415 million pension plus $19.725 million other benefits), equal to about $1.00 per share and 1.04% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If future contributions and direct benefit payments are not already captured in equity-level OE, the existing tax-adjusted deficit belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Because our other postretirement plans are unfunded, the anticipated benefits with respect to these plans will come from our own assets.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether an additional bridge deduction is required remains unresolved because pension expense and future cash funding could otherwise be double-counted. Even deducting the entire filed net deficit reduces base value by only about $1.00 per share, far short of the $26.31 gap between the $95.97 base value and the $122.28 market price, so it cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map forecast contributions and direct benefit payments to OE; if they are absent, deduct the appropriately tax-adjusted net deficit and rerun the bridge while avoiding double-counting retained pension expense.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 tax burden contains a nonrecurring benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.0 million tax benefit, equal to 4.2% of 2025 OE and 4.8% of anchor OE; a conservative dollar-for-dollar anchor adjustment would reduce bull value by about $4.69 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Retention of the reserve release inflates historical after-tax OE and potentially the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we recognized a net $ 12.0 million decrease to reserves for uncertain tax positions primarily related to certain tax credits as a result of an income tax audit settlement.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefit is demonstrated, but whether it was already removed from OE is unresolved. Even the conservative assumption that the full $12.0 million reduces the anchor dollar-for-dollar would lower, rather than reverse, the bull value of $106.15, which is already $16.13 below the market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 OE tax normalization, remove the $12.0 million reserve release and any other discrete tax items if retained, recompute the log-trend anchor, and apply a recurring forward tax rate.

audit_findings.title: Confirm the 2023 property-sale gain was purged
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.1 million pre-tax, equal to 4.6% of 2023 OE; treating the full pre-tax amount as a dollar-for-dollar anchor reduction would lower bull value by about $4.73 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the disposal gain inflates 2023 OE and the log-trend anchor; ongoing sale-leaseback rent should remain in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2023, we sold certain real estate in Canada and recognized a $12.1 million pre-tax gain on sale.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated and the filing shows it was excluded from Segment EBITDA, but that does not prove it was removed from the separate OE calculation. Even an intentionally conservative full pre-tax adjustment to the anchor would leave bull value around $101.42, still below the $122.28 market price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2023 OE reconciliation to verify removal of the gain while retaining sale-leaseback rent and maintenance investment; recompute the trend anchor if the gain remains.

audit_findings.title: Former-subsidiary lease guarantees remain senior to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 recorded liability was $9.6 million, equal to about $0.24 per share and 0.25% of base equity value; December 2025 fixed remaining base rent was $17 million, or about $0.42 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Guarantee payments not represented by recurring operating earnings reduce equity through either future OE cash outflows or a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we guaranteed the lease payments for certain property leases of a former subsidiary with expiration dates extending out to 2035.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated, and the June filing reports both a recorded liability and a guarantee-termination agreement. Even using the larger $17 million contractual payment figure as a bridge deduction would reduce base value by only about $0.42 per share, far too little to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $9.6 million liability and remaining termination installments are already reflected in forecast OE; otherwise deduct the uncovered liability in the bridge without also capitalizing the same cash outflows.
